safety_verdicts.content: Patient has tried E45 cream and antihistamines with minimal relief.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated only states 'tried OTC cream with minimal benefit' and does not capture the specific E45 cream and antihistamine trial noted in the gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Omitting the specific OTC agents tried (E45 and antihistamines) slightly reduces clinical detail but does not meaningfully change diagnosis or immediate management for suspected contact dermatitis. At most, it may lead to re-trying similar therapies or less targeted counseling.

safety_verdicts.content: Patient has no known drug allergies.
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold states NKDA; generated states allergies are 'not documented' rather than recording NKDA.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Failure to document NKDA can impair safe prescribing workflows because clinicians may assume allergy status is unknown, prompting delays or, less commonly, incomplete allergy screening before medication initiation. The direct harm is usually limited but it is medication-safety relevant.

safety_verdicts.content: Prescribed a steroid cream to be used twice daily (BD).
safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Generated includes prescribing a topical steroid but does not specify twice-daily (BD) use.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Not specifying the topical steroid frequency (BD) can lead to underuse (poor symptom control, prolonged impairment) or overuse (skin atrophy, irritant effects), especially on hands with compromised skin barrier. This is typically correctable but can cause avoidable morbidity and delayed resolution.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Gold specifies hotel work; transcript does not clearly establish 'residential' work. 'Residential' is not supported and conflicts with gold.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Misstating the setting of housekeeping work (residential vs hotel/commercial) is unlikely to alter clinical risk stratification or the core advice (avoid triggers, wear gloves, emollients/topical steroid). The impact is mainly administrative/contextual rather than clinical.

safety_verdicts.eval_reasoning: Contradicts gold (metformin) and transcript does not clearly support insulin use.
safety_verdicts.clinical_rationale: Documenting insulin when the patient is actually on metformin creates a high-risk medication discrepancy; acting on it could result in inappropriate insulin prescribing/administration, causing severe hypoglycemia, seizures, or death. It can also misclassify diabetes severity/type and distort future clinical decisions.
